decisive_items: porto-venous phase CT scan revealed compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery with a filling defect in the dilated, nonenhancing left common iliac vein
Doppler ultrasonography of the left lower extremity demonstrated extensive deep vein thrombosis
a 5-day history of gradually progressive swelling, pain, and stiffness in her left lower leg
response.rationale: CT demonstrates the characteristic left common iliac vein compression by the right common iliac artery, defining May-Thurner syndrome as the underlying cause of the acute left-sided DVT.

rejected.why: Microcytic anemia is present but incidental and does not explain the acute unilateral leg swelling or DVT.
Redundant with R3; DVT of the left lower extremity is the manifestation, not the underlying cause.
Chronic venous insufficiency would not explain acute DVT with iliac vein compression on CT.
Inherited thrombophilia is unsupported by negative antiphospholipid testing and no personal or family thrombophilia history.
Thrombophilia is unsupported by negative antibody workup; the DVT is explained by anatomic venous compression.
Cellulitis is unlikely given afebrile status, normal CRP, and ultrasound-proven DVT.
Lymphedema is contradicted by extensive DVT on ultrasound and the characteristic iliac vein compression on CT.
